subject.title: [Bug]: Preflight compaction failure permanently locks Composer into "terminated" state

question: Which failure boundary should the fix for preflight compaction use before this issue is closed?
rationale: The user-visible bug is clear, but the discussion shows a real maintainer choice between skipping only well-defined transient failures, adding UI recovery, or broadening provider-error skips in a way that could hide auth/provider misconfiguration.

options.title: Skip only retryable failures
options.body: Treat timeout, 429, and 5xx preflight compaction failures as non-fatal while preserving 400/401/403, guard, request-shape, and broad summary failures as hard errors.

options.title: Recover in the UI lifecycle
options.body: Keep gateway compaction failures hard but make preflight-originated dispatch errors restore the Composer and show an actionable retry message.

options.title: Combine gateway and UI guards
options.body: Add narrow retryable gateway skips plus a UI recovery safety net for unexpected preflight dispatch errors.

recommendation.title: Skip only retryable failures
recommendation.body: Treat timeout, 429, and 5xx preflight compaction failures as non-fatal while preserving 400/401/403, guard, request-shape, and broad summary failures as hard errors.

likelyOwner.reason: They are already mentioned in the discussion as the reviewer who gave the relevant retryability-boundary feedback.
